title: Binary heap (priority queue)
summary: A binary heap is a complete binary tree stored in an array. Min-heap: parent ≤ children. Max-heap: parent ≥ children. Operations: insert (O(log n)), extract-min/max (O(log n)), peek (O(1)), heapify (O(n)). Used for priority queues, heapsort, and Dijkstra's algorithm.

ext.summary: A binary heap is a complete binary tree stored in an array. Min-heap: parent ≤ children. Max-heap: parent ≥ children. Operations: insert (O(log n)), extract-min/max (O(log n)), peek (O(1)), heapify (O(n)). Used for priority queues, heapsort, and Dijkstra's algorithm.

structure.meaning: Complete binary tree stored in array. Parent of i = floor((i-1)/2). Left child = 2i+1. Right child = 2i+2.
Parent ≤ children. Root is the minimum.
Parent ≥ children. Root is the maximum.
Add to end, sift up (swap with parent if violates heap property).
Remove root, move last element to root, sift down (swap with smaller child if violates heap property).
Build heap from array: sift down from last internal node to root.
Build max-heap, then repeatedly extract max (swap root with last, sift down). In-place, not stable.

notes: Binary heap is the standard priority queue implementation.
Heapify is O(n) (not O(n log n)) due to the tree structure.
Heapsort is O(n log n) in-place but not stable.
Fibonacci heap has better amortized complexity but is slower in practice.
Binary heap is used in Dijkstra's algorithm, A*, and task schedulers.
